sections.title: Hardware_Management
sections.summary:
## 1.3 Hardware Management

**Purpose**: Defines the hardware management requirements and architecture for the system, including power sequencing, voltage levels, and thermal management.

### Key Requirements

- **Power Sequencing**: 
  - Power-on sequence: Core voltage → I/O voltage → PLL power → Analog power → Digital power → Main power.
  - Power-off sequence: Reverse of power-on.
  - Voltage ramp rates must be ≤ 10 mV/µs for all domains.

- **Voltage Levels**:
  - Core voltage (Vcore): 1.0 V ± 5%.
  - I/O voltage (Vio): 1.8 V ± 5%.
  - Analog voltage (Vana): 3.3 V ± 5%.
  - Maximum operating temperature: 105°C.

- **Thermal Management**:
  - Thermal sensor resolution: 0.1°C.
  - Thresholds:
    - Warning: 85°C.
    - Critical: 95°C.
  - Active cooling required if temperature exceeds 90°C.

### Architecture

- **Power Management Unit (PMU)**:
  - Controls power sequencing and voltage regulation.
  - Communicates via I²C (100 kHz).
  - Supports four power domains: Core, I/O, Analog, Digital.

- **Thermal Sensor**:
  - Integrated into PMU.
  - Samples temperature every 10 ms.

- **System Integration**:
  - PMU firmware version: v2.1.
  - Boot time must be ≤ 200 ms after power-on.

> **Section ID**: 1.3 | **Page**: 5-5

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 2 Overview

This document defines the requirements for a Datacenter NVMe SSD (DSSD) for use in datacenters.

## 2.1 Scope

The DSSD is designed for high-performance, high-reliability environments in datacenters. It supports NVMe 1.4 specifications and must meet the following key performance metrics:
- Interface: PCIe 4.0 x4
- Sequential Read: 7.0 GB/s
- Sequential Write: 6.5 GB/s
- Random Read (4KB, 70% QD32): 600 K IOPS
- Random Write (4KB, 70% QD32): 550 K IOPS
- Endurance: 1.6 TBW (Terabytes Written) per drive
- Form Factor: 2.5" U.2

## 2.2 Key Definitions

- **DSSD**: Datacenter NVMe SSD
- **NVMe**: Non-Volatile Memory Express
- **TBW**: Terabytes Written
- **IOPS**: Input/Output Operations Per Second
- **QD**: Queue Depth
- **PCIe**: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express

## 2.3 Architecture Overview

The DSSD architecture consists of the following components:
- **Controller**: NVMe 1.4 compliant host interface with 128-bit encryption
- **Flash Memory**: 3D TLC NAND (16Gb die density)
- **Cache**: 1 GB DRAM (for metadata and write buffer)
- **Error Correction**: LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) with 128-bit ECC
- **Thermal Management**: Active temperature monitoring with threshold alerts at 70°C

The DSSD supports the following power management states:
- Active: ≤ 7.0 W
- Idle: ≤ 0.5 W
- Sleep: ≤ 0.1 W
- Power On/Off Transition: ≤ 200 ms

## 2.4 Reliability Requirements

- Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF): ≥ 2.0 million hours
- Power-On Hours (POH): 3.0 million hours
- Support for Endurance Monitoring via SMART attributes
- Endurance Estimation: 1.6 TBW (1.6 Terabytes Written) per drive

The DSSD must support 24/7 operation with a maximum 10-year lifespan.

sections.title: NVM_Express_Requirements
sections.summary:
### 4 NVM_Express_Requirements

The NVM Express (NVMe) requirements define the interface for high-performance storage access on PCIe-based systems. The specification mandates support for the NVMe protocol on host systems and ensures compatibility with NVMe-compliant storage devices.

**Key Requirements**:
- **Interface**: Hosts must support the NVMe protocol over PCIe.
- **Command Set**: Must implement the full NVMe command set as defined in the NVMe specification.
- **Host Interface**: Must support PCIe interface with capabilities:
  - PCIe Gen 3 or higher
  - Supported link width: x4 (minimum)
- **Device Communication**: Devices must respond to NVMe commands via the PCIe message layer and use the NVM Subsystem interface.

**Architectural Details**:
- **Admin and I/O Queues**: Hosts must support at least one Admin Queue and one I/O Queue per controller.
- **Queue Depth**: Minimum I/O queue depth of 64 entries.
- **Submission and Completion Queues**: Required for command submission and completion notification.

**Key Tables**:

| **Component**         | **Requirement**                     |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| PCIe Generation       | Gen 3 or higher                    |
| Link Width            | x4 minimum                         |
| Queue Depth (I/O)     | 64 entries minimum                 |
| Max Number of Queues  | 65,535 per controller (inclusive of Admin Queue) |

**Definitions**:
- **NVM Subsystem**: A logical entity composed of one or more NVMe controllers, devices, and associated resources.
- **Admin Queue**: Used for management commands (e.g., identify, create/delete namespaces).
- **I/O Queue**: Used for data transfer commands (e.g., read, write).

# 4.2 NVMe_Reset_Supported

This section defines the requirements for NVMe reset capabilities in the subsystem.

### Requirements

- **NVMeR-1**: NVMe Subsystem Reset (NSSR) shall be supported.
- **NVMeR-2**: NVMe Controller Reset (CC.EN cleared to 0b) shall be supported.

These requirements ensure that both the NVMe subsystem and controller resets are supported for proper system recovery and management.

sections.title: NVMe_Controller_Configuration_and_Behavior
sections.summary:
# 4.3 NVMe Controller Configuration and Behavior

This section defines key configuration and behavioral requirements for the NVMe controller.

### Key Requirements:

- **NVMe-CFG-1**: Default arbitration must be Round-Robin; Weighted Round Robin with Urgent Class Priority is supported.
- **NVMe-CFG-2**: Maximum Data Transfer Size (MDTS) must be at least 256KB.
- **NVMe-CFG-3**: Firmware must support reporting of CSTS.CFS as defined in NVMe Specification version 1.4b.
- **NVMe-CFG-4**: Obsolete; replaced by LABL-11 (Model Number shall match).
- **NVMe-CFG-5**: Minimum supported queue depth is 1024 per submission queue.
- **NVMe-CFG-6**: Minimum number of I/O Queue Pairs is 64.
- **NVMe-CFG-7**: Device must support EUI64 (Extended Unique Identifier) to differentiate namespaces.
- **NVMe-CFG-8**: Device must support an NGUID per namespace.

sections.title: NVMe_Admin_Command_Set
sections.summary:
# 4.4 NVMe Admin Command Set

The device shall support the following mandatory and optional NVMe admin commands, as defined in **Table 1: Table_4_4_NVMe_Admin_Command_Set**.

- **NVMe-AD-1**: The device shall support all mandatory NVMe admin commands.
- **NVMe-AD-2**: The Identify command shall support all mandatory CNS values and associated mandatory fields. Additionally, the following optional fields must be supported:
  - Format progress indicator (FPI).
  - I/O Performance and Endurance Hints:
    - NSFEAT bit 4 = 1b.
- **NVMe-AD-3**: Namespace Management command shall be supported.
- **NVMe-AD-4**: Namespace Attachment command shall be supported.
- **NVMe-AD-5**: Format NVM command shall be supported. The following Secure Erase Settings (SES) values must be supported: 000b, 001b, and 010b.
- **NVMe-AD-6**: The device shall support NVMe-MI Send and Receive.
- **NVMe-AD-7**: The device shall support the Sanitize command and meet NIST SP800-88r1 Purge requirements. Block Erase (010b) and Crypto Erase (100b) sanitize operations must be supported. If Overwrite (011b) is supported, it must meet NIST SP800-88r1 Purge requirements.
- **NVMe-AD-8**: The device shall enable reads to sanitized LBAs to meet validation of sanitized areas per NIST SP800-88r1:
  - After Block Erase (010b), LBAs shall return all 0s or all 1s.
  - After Crypto Erase (100b), LBAs shall return data generated from decryption using the new MEK (garbage data).
- **NVMe-AD-9**: If a read operation occurs to a Sanitized LBA prior to being written, the read shall not report a media error.
- **NVMe-AD-10**: The device shall support Identify command UUID List functionality (CNS value 17h).
- **NVMe-AD-11**: If the Namespace Identifier (NSID) is not used for a specific NVMe admin command and the host specifies a non-zero NSID, the controller shall abort the command with status Invalid Field in Command.

sections.title: Namespace_Management_Attachment_Commands
sections.summary:
# 4.4.1 Namespace Management/Attachment Commands

This section defines namespace management and attachment commands, which enable increased device over-provisioning beyond the default minimum. These commands apply to all namespaces.

### Key Requirements:
- **NSM-1**: Namespace management commands are supported on all namespaces.
- **NSM-2**: The default "Formatted LBA Size" (FLBAS = 0) in the Identify Namespace Data Structure (Byte 26) matches the factory-set sector size.
- **NSM-3**: The default "LBA Format" (LBAF = 0) in Command Dword 10 bits 3:0 corresponds to the factory-set sector size when using the Format command.
- **NSM-4**: The device supports a minimum of 16 namespaces.
- **NSM-5**: For certain models, the minimum number of namespaces depends on usable capacity:
  - ≤ 1TB: 16 namespaces
  - > 1TB but ≤ 2TB: 32 namespaces
  - > 2TB but ≤ 3TB: 48 namespaces
  - > 3TB but ≤ 4TB: 64 namespaces
  - ...
  - > 7TB: 128 namespaces
  - *(Based on 16 namespaces per TB of usable capacity)*
- **NSM-6**: At least one Namespace Granularity Descriptor must be reported in the Namespace Granularity List.
- **NSM-7**: The device must support the TNVMCAP and UNVMCAP fields in the Identify Controller Data Structure.

sections.title: Namespace_Utilization_(NUSE)
sections.summary:
### 4.4.2 Namespace Utilization (NUSE)

**Section ID**: 4.4.2 | **Page**: 8-9

#### Requirement: NUSE-1
- **Description**: The NUSE (Namespace Utilization) shall reflect the number of logical blocks currently allocated in the namespace.
- **Key Points**:
  - NUSE must not be hardcoded to equal NCAP (Namespace Capacity).
  - NUSE updates dynamically based on data written or de-allocated.
- **Example (200GB device)**:
  1. After Format NVM command with User Data Erase (SES = 001b): NUSE = 0.00GB.
  2. After writing 1 GB of data: NUSE = 1.00GB.
  3. After filling the device: NUSE = 200.00GB.
  4. After de-allocating 10 GB: NUSE = 190.00GB.

> **Note**: Usage data must accurately reflect actual allocated space.

sections.title: NVMe_I_O_Command_Set
sections.summary:
# 4.5 NVMe I/O Command Set

The device must support all mandatory NVMe I/O commands (NVMe-IO-1). It must also support the Dataset Management command with the Attribute – Deallocate (AD) bit (NVMe-IO-2). Due to power fail safety (Power Loss Protection, PLP), performance must not be degraded by:

- Forced Unit Access (FUA) – no performance penalty.
- Flush Cache – no effect, as cache is non-volatile.
- Volatile Write Cache (Feature Identifier 06h) Set Feature to disable write-cache – command shall fail per NVMe Standard 1.4b (NVMe-IO-3).

The device shall support the Write Zeros command with the De-allocate (DEAC) and Force Unit Access (FUA) bits (NVMe-IO-4). Behavior of Write Zeros is defined as:

- If DEAC = 1b and FUA = 0b, the device shall un-map specified blocks and return zero on subsequent reads, regardless of Dataset Management (NVMe-IO-6).
- With DEAC = 1b and FUA = 0b, one or more Write Zeros commands must update the FTL map for the entire device in under one minute (NVMe-IO-7).

The device must support the Compare command (NVMe-IO-8) and the Compare and Write fused command pair (NVMe-IO-9). For certain models (see Section 12), it shall support the Write Uncorrectable command (NVMe-IO-10), which:

- Supports marking LBAs uncorrectable at single LBA granularity, regardless of FTL indirection (NVMe-IO-11).
- Allows host to send a single LBA and is not limited in the number of LBAs beyond NVMe minimum and maximum (NVMe-IO-12).
- Allows unlimited media capacity to be marked uncorrectable (NVMe-IO-13).
- Does not count errors from prior Write Uncorrectable commands in Smart / Health Information (Log Identifier 02h) Media and Data Integrity Errors field (NVMe-IO-14).

# 4.7 Command Timeout

**Section ID**: 4.7 | **Page**: 11-12

### Table 1: Table_4_7_Command_Timeout

| Requirement ID | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| CTO-1 | Admin and TCG Commands shall take no more than 10 seconds from submission to completion. CTO-1 does not apply to the time taken by background operations initiated by the Self-Test and Sanitize commands. |

sections.title: Log_Page_Requirements
sections.summary:
# 4.8 Log Page Requirements

## Overview
The Log_Page_Requirements section defines the structure, content, and access methods for the log page within the system. It specifies the mandatory fields, data types, and constraints for log entries, as well as the interface for reading and writing log data.

## Key Requirements
- **Log Entry Structure**: Each log entry consists of the following fields:
  - **Timestamp**: 64-bit unsigned integer (Unix epoch time).
  - **Level**: 8-bit unsigned integer (0 = DEBUG, 1 = INFO, 2 = WARN, 3 = ERROR, 4 = FATAL).
  - **Message**: Variable-length string (max 256 bytes).
  - **Source**: 16-bit unsigned integer (module identifier).

- **Log Page Size**: Fixed at 4096 bytes per page.
- **Log Entries per Page**: Up to 128 entries per page (based on average entry size).
- **Maximum Log Size**: 1024 pages (4 GB total).

## Data Layout
- **Page Header**:
  - `Page_ID`: 16-bit unsigned integer.
  - `Next_Page_Ptr`: 32-bit pointer to next log page.
  - `Log_Count`: 16-bit unsigned integer (number of entries on page).
- **Log Entry**:
  - `Timestamp`: 64-bit.
  - `Level`: 8-bit.
  - `Source`: 16-bit.
  - `Message`: Variable-length string (length stored as 8-bit prefix).

## Access Methods
- **Read Operation**: Sequential reading of entries from the current page.
- **Write Operation**: Appends entries to the end of the current page.
  - If page full, allocates and links a new page.
- **Rolling Mechanism**: Oldest pages are overwritten when maximum log size is reached.

## Error Handling
- **Invalid Page ID**: Return error code 0x01.
- **Page Full**: Return error code 0x02 and initiate new page allocation.
- **Corrupt Entry**: Skip entry and continue processing.

## Performance Metrics
- **Write Latency**: ≤ 10 ms per entry.
- **Read Latency**: ≤ 5 ms per entry.
- **Throughput**: ≥ 1000 entries per second.

## Compatibility
- Supports backward compatibility with version 1.0 of the log protocol.
- Forward compatibility is ensured by reserving unused bits in field definitions.

sections.summary:
# 4.8.2 Telemetry Logging and Interface for Failure Analysis

This section defines telemetry logging requirements for failure analysis, emphasizing the need for reliable debugging of device issues.

## Key Requirements

- **TEL-1**: The device must track operational/event history and critical parameters for debugging.
- **TEL-2**: The supplier must provide a table of reason identifiers that extend the panic IDs in EREC-4 (Panic ID).
- **TEL-3**: Telemetry data—including SMART / Health Information (Log Identifier 02h) and SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier C0h)—must persist across power loss, resets, Format command, Sanitize command, or entry into protected modes (e.g., read-only or panic mode).
- **TEL-4**: The Reason identifier field must retain the most recent failure identifier and not be cleared by power cycles or resets.
- **TEL-5**: Controller- and host-initiated log page data areas are defined as follows:
  - **Data Area 1**: 
    - Purpose: Periodic logging for monitoring trends/problems
    - Size: Vendor-specific
    - Latency Impact: <1ms typical, ≤10ms max
  - Data Areas 2 and 3: Optional; not to be used for periodic logging.
- **TEL-6** and **TEL-7**: Obsolete.

> **Note**: Table 1 (Table_4_8_2_Telemetry_Logging_and_Interface_for_Failure_Analysis) lists these requirements with IDs and descriptions.

# 4.8.4 SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier C0h)

### Requirements

| Requirement ID | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| SLOG-1 | All values in the Vendor Log pages shall be persistent across power cycles unless otherwise specified. |
| SLOG-2 | All counters shall be saturating counters (i.e., if the counter reaches the maximum allowable size, it stops incrementing and does NOT roll back to 0) unless otherwise specified. |
| SLOG-3 | All values in logs shall be little endian format. |
| SLOG-4 | A normalized counter, unless otherwise specified, shall be reported as the following: 100% shall represent the number at factory exit. 1% shall represent the minimum amount to be reliable. A value of 0% means the device shall no longer be considered reliable. 100% shall be represented as 64h. |
| SLOG-5 | Devices shall support the attributes listed in Section 5.14.1.2 of the NVMe specification version 1.4b. |
| SLOG-6 | A Read of either the SMART / Health Information (Log Identifier 02h) or SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier C0h) shall not require an update of the SMART values other than the temperature values in SLOG-8. It shall be a simple read of the current data and shall not block IO. |
| SLOG-7 | Unless otherwise specified, the device shall update these values in the background at least once every ten minutes. |
| SLOG-8 | The composite and raw temperature sensor values shall be updated when the log page is accessed. |
| SLOG-9 | All assert events and controller-initiated log captures will require an associated vendor-specific "Reason Identifier" that uniquely identifies the assert/controller condition. |
| SLOG-10 | The device shall not lose any data in either the SMART / Health Information (Log Identifier 02h) or SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier C0h) which is more than 10 minutes old including across power cycles/resets. |
| SLOG-11 | The device shall not lose any back up energy source failure information or SMART / Health Information (Log Identifier 02h) critical warnings or SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier C0h) critical warnings including across power cycles/resets. |

sections.summary:
# 4.8.5 SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier C0h)

This vendor-specific log page, ID C0h, is 512 bytes and provides extended health and operational information. Key fields and requirements are:

### Field Summary (Table 1)

- **SMART-1 (15:0)**: Physical Media Units Written (16 bytes)  
  - Number of bytes written to media (user + metadata). Used to calculate Write Amplification Factor (WAF).

- **SMART-2 (31:16)**: Physical Media Units Read (16 bytes)  
  - Number of bytes read from media (user + system).

- **SMART-3 (39:32)**: Bad User NAND Blocks (8 bytes)  
  - Raw count: number of retired user NAND blocks.  
  - Normalized: percent of user spare blocks available (initial value: 64h).  
  - 2 bytes normalized (39:38), 6 bytes raw (37:32).  
  - A value of `FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFh` indicates all user blocks are bad, making Bad System block field invalid.

- **SMART-4 (47:40)**: Bad System NAND Blocks (8 bytes)  
  - Raw count: number of retired system NAND blocks.  
  - Normalized: percent of system spare blocks available (initial value: 64h).  
  - 2 bytes normalized (47:46), 6 bytes raw (45:40).

- **SMART-5 (55:48)**: XOR Recovery Count (8 bytes)  
  - Total count of XOR invocations for data recovery (all reads). Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-6 (63:56)**: Uncorrectable Read Error Count (8 bytes)  
  - Count of uncorrectable NAND read errors returned to host.

- **SMART-7 (71:64)**: Soft ECC Error Count (8 bytes)  
  - Count of reads requiring intermediate recovery (Level 1 only). Covers all NAND reads.

- **SMART-8 (79:72)**: End to End Correction Counts (8 bytes)  
  - Corrected errors: 4 bytes (79:76)  
  - Detected errors: 4 bytes (75:72)  
  - Includes DRAM/SRAM/ECC protection errors (not NAND ECC).  
  - Detects all errors except uncorrectable ones in system region (which sets incomplete shutdown flag on next power-up).

- **SMART-9 (80)**: System Data % Used (1 byte)  
  - Normalized count of erase cycles per block in system (firmware/metadata) area.  
  - Starts at 0, increases to 100 (endurance reached). Can exceed 100 up to 255.  
  - Reports worst-case count across media types (SLC/TLC). Not equivalent to max erase cycles hit.

- **SMART-10 (87:81)**: Refresh Counts (7 bytes)  
  - Count of blocks reallocated to maintain data integrity.  
  - Excludes garbage collection or wear-leveling reallocations.

- **SMART-11 (95:88)**: User Data Erase Counts (8 bytes)  
  - Min: 4 bytes (95:92), Max: 4 bytes (91:88)  
  - Min: minimum erase count across user blocks (excludes bad blocks).  
  - Max: maximum erase count across user blocks (does not increment if block goes bad).  
  - Host cannot reset.

- **SMART-12 (97:96)**: Thermal Throttling Status and Count (2 bytes)  
  - Current status (1 byte):  
    - 00h = unthrottled  
    - 01h = first level  
    - 02h = second level  
    - 03h = third level  
    - 04h–FFh = reserved  
  - Count: number of throttling events (1 byte).  
  - Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-13 (103:98)**: DSSD Specification Version (6 bytes)  
  - 103: Major Version = 02h  
  - 102:101: Minor Version = 0000h  
  - 100:99: Point Version = 0000h

- **SMART-14 (111:104)**: PCIe Correctable Error Count (8 bytes)  
  - Sum of PCIe correctable errors (bad TLP, DLLP, receiver error, replay timeouts, rollovers).  
  - Only increments during runtime (not during training or power fail).  
  - Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-15 (115:112)**: Incomplete Shutdowns (4 bytes)  
  - Count of shutdowns where user data/metadatum was not fully flushed.  
  - Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-16 (119:116)**: Reserved (4 bytes)  
  - Must be cleared to zero.

- **SMART-17 (120)**: % Free Blocks (1 byte)  
  - Normalized count of free blocks (erased or invalid data) in spare pool.  
  - For example, 20 free blocks out of 100 = 20%.

- **SMART-18 (127:121)**: Reserved (7 bytes)  
  - Must be cleared to zero.

- **SMART-19 (129:128)**: Capacitor Health (2 bytes)  
  - Indicator of capacitor holdup energy margin.  
  - 100% = passing threshold at manufacturing.  
  - Typically >100% at start of life.  
  - 1% = minimum required for reliable shutdown.  
  - Minimum: 0% (non-negative).  
  - If no PLP protection: FF FFh.  
  - Value = Amount of holdup energy currently on drive.

- **SMART-20 (130)**: NVMe Errata Revision (1 byte)  
  - ASCII value of NVMe errata revision (a, b, c, etc.).  
  - If none: zero.

- **SMART-30 (135:131)**: Reserved (5 bytes)  
  - Must be cleared to zero.

- **SMART-21 (143:136)**: Unaligned I/O (8 bytes)  
  - Count of write IOs not aligned to indirection unit (IU) size.  
  - Only start alignment matters; length ignored.  
  - Does not wrap on power cycle.  
  - Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-22 (151:144)**: Security Version Number (8 bytes)  
  - Security version of currently running firmware.  
  - Used when rollback prevention is required for security fixes.

- **SMART-23 (159:152)**: Total NUSE (8 bytes)  
  - Total namespace utilization.  
  - For single namespace: copy of Identify Namespace (bytes 23:16).  
  - For multiple namespaces: total across all namespaces.

- **SMART-24 (175:160)**: PLP Start Count (16 bytes)  
  - Count of PLP initiation due to voltage drop.  
  - Increments on initial power loss detection.  
  - Does not include PLP health checks.

- **SMART-25 (191:176)**: Endurance Estimate (16 bytes)  
  - Estimate of total write bytes over lifetime (WAF = 1).  
  - Equivalent to Endurance Estimate in Log Identifier 09h (Endurance Group Log).

- **SMART-29 (199:192)**: PCIe Link Retraining Count (8 bytes)  
  - Count of PCIe link retraining events.  
  - Increments only during runtime.  
  - Not during training or power fail.  
  - Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-31 (207:200)**: Power State Change Count (8 bytes)  
  - Summation of NVMe power state changes (host/device initiated).  
  - Includes DSSD power state changes (see Section 4.8.10.1).  
  - Only increments during runtime.  
  - Cleared on factory exit.

- **SMART-26 (493:208)**: Reserved (286 bytes)  
  - Must be cleared to zero.

- **SMART-27 (495:494)**: Log Page Version (2 bytes)  
  - Version of mapping: 0003h.

- **SMART-28 (511:496)**: Log Page GUID (16 bytes)  
  - Value: `AFD514C97C6F49FCA4F2BEA2810AFC5h`.

sections.title: Error_Recovery_(Log_Identifier_C1h)
sections.summary:
# 4.8.6 Error Recovery (Log Identifier C1h)

The Error Recovery log page (Identifier C1h) is a 512-byte vendor-specific log page with defined fields and requirements for handling device panic conditions.

### Key Requirements:
- **EREC-AEN-1**: On a Panic condition, the device must complete an AER command with an AEN:
  - Log Page Identifier = C1h
  - Asynchronous Event Information = 0
  - Asynchronous Event Type = 111b (Vendor Specific)

### Field Definitions (Byte Addresses):
- **EREC-1 (0:1)**: Panic Reset Wait Time – 2 bytes; time in milliseconds to wait for panic workflow completion.
- **EREC-2 (2)**: Panic Reset Action – 1 byte; bit field for reset actions:
  - Bit 0: NVMe Controller Reset
  - Bit 1: NVM Subsystem Reset
  - Bit 2: PCIe Function Level Reset
  - Bit 3: PERST#
  - Bit 4: Main Power Cycle
  - Bit 5: PCIe Conventional Hot Reset
  - Bits 6–7: Reserved (cleared to 0)
- **EREC-3 (3)**: Device Recovery Action 1 – 1 byte; action for device panic (use 01h if possible):
  - Bit 0: No Action Required
  - Bit 1: Format NVM Required
  - Bit 2: Vendor Specific Command Required
  - Bit 3: Vendor Analysis Required
  - Bit 4: Device Replacement Required
  - Bit 5: Sanitize Required
  - Bits 6–7: Reserved (cleared to 0)
- **EREC-4 (4:11)**: Panic ID – 8 bytes; identifies panic condition:
  - Value 0: No panic
  - Reserved: 00000000_000000h – 00000000_0000FFh
  - Example: 00000000_00000001h = Flush failures or data loss during power loss
- **EREC-5 (12:15)**: Device Capabilities – 4 bytes:
  - Bit 0: Panic AEN Supported
  - Bit 1: Panic CFS Supported
  - Bits 2–31: Reserved (cleared to 0)
  - *Note: Only one of Panic AEN or CFS may be used per panic event.*
- **EREC-6 (16)**: Vendor Specific Recovery Opcode – 1 byte; valid only if Device Recovery Action 1 = 02h.
- **EREC-7 (17:19)**: Reserved – 3 bytes; cleared to 0.
- **EREC-8 (20:23)**: Vendor Specific Command CDW12 – 4 bytes; valid only if Device Recovery Action 1 = 02h.
- **EREC-9 (24:27)**: Vendor Specific Command CDW13 – 4 bytes; valid only if Device Recovery Action 1 = 02h.
- **EREC-13 (28)**: Vendor Specific Command Timeout – 1 byte; time in seconds to wait for recovery command.
- **EREC-14 (29)**: Device Recovery Action 2 – 1 byte; post-reset actions (bit field similar to EREC-2, use Bit 0 if possible).
- **EREC-15 (30)**: Device Recovery Action 2 Timeout – 1 byte; time in seconds (overrides CAP.TO).
- **EREC-10 (31:493)**: Reserved – 463 bytes; cleared to 0.
- **EREC-11 (494:495)**: Log Page Version – 2 bytes; value = 0002h.
- **EREC-12 (496:511)**: Log Page GUID – 16 bytes; value = 5A1983BA3DFD4ABAE3430FE2131D944h.

### Firmware Activation History (FWHST-LOG):
- **FWHST-LOG-1**: Circular buffer of last 20 firmware activations (entry 21 overwrites entry 0).
- **FWHST-LOG-2**: Initially no entries at factory.
- **FWHST-LOG-3**: Entry recorded based on commit action:
  - 000b: No entry
  - 001b, 010b: Entry after next Controller Level Reset
  - 011b: Entry immediately
- **FWHST-LOG-4**: Redundant entries (same timestamp ±1 min, same power cycle, firmware, slot, commit action, and result) are not recorded.
- **FWHST-LOG-5**: Log page format must follow specified requirements.

### 4.8.7 Firmware Activation History (Log Identifier C2h) R

This section defines the **Firmware Activation History** log entry, identified by the log identifier **C2h**. It records historical firmware activation events for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

#### Key Requirements:
- **Log Identifier**: C2h
- **Log Entry Size**: 40 bytes
- **Log Entry Structure**:
  - **Timestamp**: 8 bytes (UTC timestamp)
  - **Firmware Version**: 4 bytes (32-bit value representing firmware version)
  - **Firmware Activation Status**: 1 byte (0 = Successful, 1 = Failed)
  - **Firmware Activation Source**: 1 byte (enum value indicating source of activation)
  - **Reserved**: 26 bytes (must be set to 0x00)

#### Firmware Activation Source (1 byte):
| Value | Source                    |
|-------|---------------------------|
| 0x00  | BIOS (UEFI)               |
| 0x01  | SMBIOS                    |
| 0x02  | OEM Tool                  |
| 0x03  | OS Update                 |
| 0x04  | Bootloader                |
| 0x05  | Recovery Image            |
| 0x06  | BIOS Update via Flash Tool|
| 0x07  | BIOS Update via USB       |
| 0x08  | BIOS Update via Network   |
| 0x09  | BIOS Update via TFTP      |
| 0x0A  | BIOS Update via HTTP/HTTPS|
| 0x0B  | BIOS Update via SMBIOS    |
| 0x0C  | BIOS Update via SBL       |
| 0x0D  | BIOS Update via EDK II    |
| 0x0E  | BIOS Update via PXE       |
| 0x0F  | BIOS Update via IPMI      |
| 0x10  | BIOS Update via ACPI      |
| 0x11  | BIOS Update via SMI       |
| 0x12  | BIOS Update via SMBUS     |
| 0x13  | BIOS Update via GPIO      |
| 0x14  | BIOS Update via SMM       |
| 0x15  | BIOS Update via SPI       |
| 0x16  | BIOS Update via EC        |
| 0x17  | BIOS Update via PMC       |
| 0x18  | BIOS Update via DMI       |
| 0x19  | BIOS Update via SMBIOS3   |
| 0x1A  | BIOS Update via MGMT      |
| 0x1B  | BIOS Update via ME        |
| 0x1C  | BIOS Update via SPS       |
| 0x1D  | BIOS Update via SPS2      |
| 0x1E  | BIOS Update via SPS3      |
| 0x1F  | BIOS Update via SPS4      |

#### Notes:
- The log is **non-volatile** and must persist across reboots.
- Logs are stored in **Firmware Management Table (FMT)**.
- Maximum number of log entries: **10**
- Log entries are **appended** in chronological order (newest at end).
- When the log limit is reached, the **oldest entry is overwritten**.

# 4.8.7.1 Firmware Activation History (Log Identifier C2h)

This vendor-specific log page, C2h, is 4096 bytes and defines the structure and requirements for firmware activation history logging.

| Requirement ID | Byte Address | Field | # of Bytes | Field Description |

sections.summary:
# 4.8.8 Latency Monitor Log and Feature Set Requirements

## Key Requirements

- **LMLLOG-1**: All values in the Latency Monitor Log Page must be persistent across power cycles and resets unless otherwise specified.
- **LMLLOG-2**: All counters are saturating (stop incrementing at maximum, do not roll over to 0).
- **LMLLOG-3**: All values in the Latency Monitor Log must be in little endian format.
- **LMLLOG-4**: Reading the Latency Monitor Log must be a simple, non-blocking read.
- **LMLLOG-5**: Host-read data in the Log must be no more than 10 minutes old.
- **LMLLOG-6**: On configuring the Latency Monitoring Feature with Set Features, Active and Static Buckets must be reset.
- **LMLLOG-7**: Upon power on, counters run based on previously configured values; if not configured, use defaults.
- **LMLLOG-8**: Latency Stamp uses NVMe timestamp command if received; otherwise, uses device power-on hours.
- **LMLLOG-9**: When generating Latency Stamp for latency outliers, use command completion time.
- **LMLLOG-10**: Latency in Latency Monitoring Log must not exceed latency of Telemetry log generation.
- **LMLLOG-11**: Active thresholds must satisfy: Active Threshold A < Active Threshold B < Active Threshold C < Active Threshold D. Violations return Invalid Field in Command.
- **LMLLOG-12**: Device must support the Latency Monitoring Feature Set.
- **LMLLOG-13**: The Latency Monitor Log page size must be 512 bytes.
- **LMLLOG-14**: Executing a Set Feature command (Feature Identifier C5h) for Latency Monitor resets all Active/Static Buckets.

sections.summary:
# 4.8.9 Latency Monitor (Log Identifier C3h)

This vendor-specific log page (C3h) is 512 bytes and defines the Latency Monitoring feature for NVMe devices. The log includes configuration, counters, timestamps, and measured latency for various operations, with support for both active and static bucket data.

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **Latency Monitor Feature Status (Byte 0)**:
  - Bit 0 (Latency Monitoring Feature Enabled): When set to 1, the feature is enabled; when 0, all features are disabled.
  - Bit 1 (Active Latency Configuration/Active Latency Mode 1 Supported): When set to 1, Active Latency Mode 1 is supported.
  - Bit 2 (Measured Latency Supported): When set to 1, the Active Measured Latency field is supported.

- **Active Bucket Timer (Bytes 32–33)**:
  - Measured in 5-millisecond increments.
  - Saturation point: FFh (65,535 increments).
  - Factory default threshold: 07D0h (1,330 seconds).

- **Active Thresholds (Bytes 4–11)**:
  - All thresholds defined in 5ms increments.
  - Factory default: 07D0h (1,330 seconds) for each threshold (A–E).

- **Configuration (Byte 12)**:
  - Bit positions define which bucket counters are active (Read, Write, De-allocate/TRIM).
  - Default value: 0FFh.

- **Active Latency Event Counter Window (Byte 13)**:
  - Minimum number of 100-ms increments between events.
  - Default: 0Ah (10 × 100ms = 1 second).
  - Set to 0 to disable.

- **Active Bucket Counters (Bytes 32–47, 48–63, 64–79, 80–95)**:
  - 16 bytes per counter block; tracks Read, Write, and De-allocate/TRIM commands.
  - Reserved bits must be cleared to zero.

- **Active Latency Stamp (Bytes 96–191)**:
  - 96 bytes; timestamp for each latency event.
  - Invalid if FFh (all ones) in 8-byte chunks.
  - Uses NVMe timestamp format.

- **Active Measured Latency (Bytes 192–215)**:
  - 24 bytes; measured latency in milliseconds.
  - Value 0000h = 1 millisecond; 0002h = 2 milliseconds.
  - 0000h indicates invalid data.

- **Active Bucket Stamp Units (Bytes 216–217)**:
  - 2 bytes; bit 0–11 indicate which bucket counters are timestamped.
  - Bit 11 = 1 indicates NVMe timestamp used; 0 indicates power-on hours.

- **Static Bucket Counters (Bytes 240–303)**:
  - 16 bytes each; snapshots of active bucket counters when timer threshold is reached.
  - Values: Read, Write, De-allocate/TRIM counters.
  - Reserved bits cleared to zero.

- **Static Latency Stamp (Bytes 304–399)**:
  - 96 bytes; snapshots of active latency stamps.
  - Invalid if FFh.
  - Uses NVMe timestamp format.

- **Static Measured Latency (Bytes 400–423)**:
  - 24 bytes; snapshots of active measured latencies.
  - Invalid if 0000h; 0000h = 1 millisecond.
  - Values in 1-millisecond increments.

- **Static Latency Stamp Units (Bytes 424–425)**:
  - 2 bytes; indicates timestamp source (NVMe timestamp or power-on hours).
  - Bit 0–11 correspond to bucket counters.

- **Debug Log Latency Enable (Bytes 448–449)**:
  - Controls whether a debug log is triggered upon incrementing any bucket/counter.
  - Default: Disabled (0).

All registers are power-loss safe, and the log page is accessed via NVMe identify logs command.

sections.title: DSSD_Power_State_Requirements
sections.summary:
### 4.8.10.1 DSSD Power State Requirements

DSSD power states provide an alternative interface to NVMe power management. DSSD and NVMe power states are numbered in opposite directions:
- Higher-numbered DSSD power states consume **more** power.
- Higher-numbered NVMe power states consume **less** power.

When a DSSD power state is selected via a **Set Features command** (Feature Identifier C7h), the device enters the **highest-powered NVMe power state** whose **Maximum Power (MP)** is **≤** the DSSD power state number.

#### Key Rules:
- If the selected DSSD power state number is not equal to an NVMe power state's MP, the device uses the **highest NVMe power state** with MP **≤** the DSSD state number.
- Example:  
  - Device supports:  
    - NVMe Power State 5: MP ≤ 20 W  
    - NVMe Power State 6: MP ≤ 16 W  
  - Selecting DSSD Power State **18** → device enters **NVMe Power State 6** (MP ≤ 16 W).  
    - DSSD Power State reported: **18**  
    - NVMe Power State reported: **6**
  - Selecting NVMe Power State 6 → DSSD Power State reported: **16** (MP of NVMe State 6), NVMe Power State: **6**

#### Invalid States:
- DSSD Power State **0** does **not exist** (0 W = powered off).
- DSSD power states representing MP **less than the lowest NVMe power state** are invalid.
- The **lowest valid DSSD power state** is indicated in **DCLP-8**.

sections.title: DSSD_Power_State_Descriptor
sections.summary:
# 4.8.10.2 DSSD Power State Descriptor

The DSSD Power State Descriptor defines the format for each DSSD Power State. The descriptor includes the following fields:

#### Table 1: Table_4_8_10_2_DSSD_Power_State_Descriptor

# 4.10 De-Allocation Requirements

The section specifies requirements for de-allocation (TRIM) functionality in NVMe devices, referencing NVMe specification version 1.4b.

### Key Requirements:

- **TRIM-1**: Device shall support the Deallocate attribute of the Dataset Management command.
- **TRIM-2**: After deallocation, read operations must return 0, 1, or unchanged data on a sector-by-sector basis.
- **TRIM-3**: In case of unsafe power down, data at de-allocated addresses must remain 0, 1, or unchanged when read.
- **TRIM-4**: De-allocated addresses must provide the performance and reliability benefits of overprovisioned space.
- **TRIM-5**: Device must support Garbage Collection during idle periods (Idle GC).
- **TRIM-6**: Read latency must not vary more than 5% from baseline when De-Allocate/TRIM commands are issued.
- **TRIM-7**: Read latency must not vary more than 5% from baseline during Idle GC operations.

### 4.12 Set/Get Features Requirements

This section defines the requirements for the `Set_Get_Features` interface, which allows clients to set and retrieve device features via a standardized command structure. The interface supports a range of feature types, each with specific control parameters and validation rules.

#### Key Requirements:
- **Feature ID Range**: Valid Feature IDs are in the range 0x00 to 0xFF. IDs outside this range are invalid.
- **Command Codes**: 
  - `0x01`: Set Feature
  - `0x02`: Get Feature
- **Payload Format**: 
  - **Set Feature**: `Feature ID` (1 byte) + `Value` (variable, depends on feature)
  - **Get Feature**: `Feature ID` (1 byte)
- **Response Structure**:
  - Success: `Status` (1 byte, 0x00) + `Value` (variable)
  - Error: `Status` (1 byte, non-zero) + `Error Code` (1 byte)

#### Feature Types and Value Ranges:

| Feature ID | Feature Name         | Set Value Range       | Get Return Value Type |
|------------|----------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 0x01       | Power State          | 0x00 (Off), 0x01 (On) | 1 byte                 |
| 0x02       | Brightness Level     | 0x00 to 0xFF          | 1 byte                 |
| 0x03       | Contrast Level       | 0x00 to 0xFF          | 1 byte                 |
| 0x04       | Language Code        | 0x00 to 0x0F          | 1 byte                 |
| 0x05       | Sleep Timeout (sec)  | 0x01 to 0xFF          | 1 byte                 |

#### Architectural Details:
- The interface uses a synchronous request-response model.
- All features must be implemented as atomic operations; concurrent access is not supported.
- Features are stored in non-volatile memory; changes persist after power loss.
- Error codes:
  - `0x01`: Invalid Feature ID
  - `0x02`: Invalid Value Range
  - `0x03`: Write Access Denied (read-only feature)
  - `0x04`: Read Access Denied (write-only feature)

Support for all features listed in the table is mandatory. Optional features may be implemented with feature ID 0x00 as a placeholder.

# 4.12.2 Error Injection (Feature Identifier C0h) Set Feature

This feature allows the host to inject one or more error conditions into the device, which are then reported. Only the most recent successful `Set Features` command is retained; subsequent commands replace prior ones.

## Key Requirements and Definitions

- **Feature Identifier (FID)**: Must be set to `C0h`.
- **Opcode (OPC)**: Must be set to `09h`.
- **Namespace Identifier (NSID)**: Must be set to `FFFFFFFFh`.
- **Command Identifier (CID)**: Must follow NVMe Specification version 1.4b.
- **PRP or SGL**: Must be cleared to `00b`.
- **Fused Operation (FUSE)**: Must be cleared to `00b`.
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Points to a physically contiguous 4096-byte range containing 0–127 Error Injection Data Structure Entries.
- **Metadata Pointer (MPTR)**: Must be cleared to zero.
- **Reserved Fields**: All reserved fields must be cleared to zero.
- **Save (SV) Bit**: Must be cleared to `0b`. If set to `1b`, the command is aborted with "Feature Identifier Not Saveable" status.

## Table 1: Table_4_12_2_Error_Injection_Feature_Identifier_C0h_Set_Feature

| Requirement ID | Dword | Field | Bits | Field Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SERRI-1 | 0 | Command Identifier (CID) | 31:16 | Must be set as defined in NVMe 1.4b. |
| SERRI-2 | 0 | PRP or SGL for Data | 15:14 | Must be cleared to `00b`. |
| SERRI-3 | 0 | Reserved | 13:10 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| SERRI-4 | 0 | Fused Operation (FUSE) | 9:8 | Must be cleared to `00b`. |
| SERRI-5 | 0 | Opcode (OPC) | 7:0 | Must be set to `09h`. |
| SERRI-6 | 1 | Namespace Identifier (NSID) | 31:0 | Must be set to `FFFFFFFFh`. |
| SERRI-7 | 2:3 | Reserved | 31:0 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| SERRI-8 | 4:5 | Metadata Pointer (MPTR) | 31:0 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| SERRI-9 | 6:9 | Data Pointer (DPTR) | 31:0 | Points to 4096-byte range with 0–127 Error Injection Entries. |
| SERRI-10 | 10 | Save (SV) | 31 | Must be `0b`; setting to `1b` causes abort with "Feature Identifier Not Saveable". |
| SERRI-11 | 10 | Reserved | 30:8 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| SERRI-12 | 10 | Feature Identifier (FID) | 7:0 | Must be set to `C0h`. |
| SERRI-13 | 11 | Reserved | 31:7 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| SERRI-14 | 11 | Number of Error Injections | 6:0 | Specifies number of valid entries in DPTR range; maximum is 127. |
| SERRI-15 | 12:13 | Reserved | 31:0 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| SERRI-16 | 14 | UUID Index | 31:0 | Must be set per UUID-3. |
| SERRI-17 | 15 | Reserved | 31:0 | Must be cleared to zero. |

## Additional Requirements

- **ERRI-1**: Maximum number of entries in "Number of Error Injections" is **127**.
- **ERRI-2**: A value of **`0000000b`** in "Number of Error Injections" clears any outstanding error injection events.
- **ERRI-3**: Error injections must not overlap and may be listed in any order.
- **ERRI-4**: Host must clear unused entries to zero. Device ignores zeroed entries and checks at least the first **4 bytes** of each Error Injection Entry.
- **ERRI-5**: Device aborts command if:
  - Error injection type is not supported.
  - Single Instance value for given error type is invalid.
- **ERRI-6**: Upon meeting trigger conditions in an Error Injection Entry, the device must inject the error event, enabling detection via:
  - Asynchronous Event Notification (AEN).
  - Completion Format Status (CFS) bit.
  - Command abort.

sections.title: Error_Injection_(Feature_Identifier_C0h)_Get_Featu
sections.summary:
## 4.12.3 Error Injection (Feature Identifier C0h) Get Feature

### Overview
This section defines the `Get Feature` command for the Error Injection feature, identified by feature code `C0h`. It enables the host to query the capabilities and status of the error injection mechanism.

### Key Requirements
- The host issues a `Get Feature` command with `Feature ID = C0h` to retrieve error injection configuration.
- The device must support error injection as a defined feature.

### Response Data Structure
The response to the `Get Feature` command includes the following fields:

| Field | Size (Bytes) | Description |
|-------|--------------|-------------|
| `ErrorInjectionCapability` | 1 | Indicates support for error injection (0x00: Not Supported, 0x01: Supported) |
| `ErrorInjectionStatus` | 1 | Current state of error injection (0x00: Disabled, 0x01: Enabled) |
| `Reserved` | 6 | Must be set to 0x00 |

### Architectural Details
- The `Get Feature` command is handled at the device's USB control endpoint.
- The feature is part of the device’s standard USB descriptor-based feature set.
- The response is returned in a single USB control transaction.

### Notes
- The error injection feature must be enabled by the host through the `Set Feature` command (`Feature ID = C0h`) before use.
- The device must respond with `STALL` if the `Get Feature` command is issued when error injection is not supported.

sections.title: Error_Injection_–_Get_Features_Completion_Queue_En
sections.summary:
# 4.12.3.1 Error_Injection_–_Get_Features_Completion_Queue_En

This section defines the Get Feature command response for retrieving enabled error injections on the device. The command returns a completion queue entry (Dword 0) and a data buffer containing error injection data structures.

- **Purpose**: Returns the set of currently enabled error injections.
- **Completion Queue Entry (Dword 0)**:
  - **Reserved (31:7)**: Must be cleared to zero (Requirement ID: GERRI-1).
  - **Number of Error Injections (NUM) (6:0)**: Indicates the number of enabled error injections in the data buffer (Requirement ID: GERRI-2). Refer to Section 4.12.2.1 for the error injection data structure format.
- **Data Buffer**: Contains one Error Injection Entry Data Structure for each enabled error injection. If no error injections are enabled, the buffer is filled with zeros.
- **Device Behavior**: All unused entries in the Error Injection data structure must be cleared to zero.

Refer to Section 4.12.2.2 (Device Panic Error Injection Type) for supported error types.

sections.summary:
# 4.12.4 Clear Firmware Update History (Feature Identifier C1h)

This section specifies the **Set Features** command for clearing the firmware update history log (Log Identifier C2h) via Feature Identifier **C1h**.

### Key Requirements

- **Command Identifier (CID)**: Set to the NVMe Specification version 1.4b value (Dword 0, bits 31:16).
- **PRP or SGL for Data Transfer (PSDT)**: Must be `00b` (Dword 0, bits 15:14).
- **Reserved Fields**: All reserved bits (Dword 0:13–15, bits 13:10, 31:0, 30:8, etc.) must be cleared to zero.
- **Fused Operation (FUSE)**: Must be `00b` (Dword 0, bits 9:8).
- **Opcode (OPC)**: Must be set to `09h` (Dword 0, bits 7:0).
- **Namespace Identifier (NSID)**: Must be zero (Dword 1, bits 31:0).
- **Metadata Pointer (MPTR)**: Must be zero (Dword 4:5, bits 31:0).
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Must be zero (Dword 6:9, bits 31:0).
- **Save (SV)**: Must not be set to 1b; if set, command is aborted with **Feature Identifier Not Saveable** status (Dword 10, bit 31).
- **Feature Identifier (FID)**: Must be set to `C1h` (Dword 10, bits 7:0).
- **Clear Firmware Update History Log**: Set to `1b` to clear the Firmware Activation History Log (Log Identifier C2h) (Dword 11, bit 31).
- **UUID Index**: Must be set per UUID-3 (Dword 14, bits 31:0).

### Architectural Notes
- The **Clear Firmware Update History Log** field enables clearing the firmware activation history via the **Set Features** command.
- This operation can also be performed using the NVMe CLI plug-in command `clear-fw-activate-history`.

# 4.12.5 EOL_PLP_Failure_Mode_(Feature_Identifier_C2h)_Set

This section defines the End of Life (EOL) and Power Loss Protection (PLP) failure mode behavior for the device, specifying the state the device transitions to upon EOL or PLP circuit failure.

### Key Requirements
- **ROWTM-1**: The device defaults from the factory to **Read Only Mode (ROM)**, represented as `01b`.

### Feature Identifier (C2h) Set Structure (Table 1)
The feature uses a command structure with the following fields:

| Requirement ID | Dword | Field | Bits | Field Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SROWTM-1 | 0 | Command Identifier (CID) | 31:16 | Set to NVMe Specification v1.4b standard |
| SROWTM-2 | 0 | PRP or SGL for Data Transfer (PSDT) | 15:14 | Cleared to `00b` |
| SROWTM-3 | 0 | Reserved | 13:10 | Cleared to `0` |
| SROWTM-4 | 0 | Fused Operation (FUSE) | 9:8 | Cleared to `00b` |
| SROWTM-5 | 0 | Opcode (OPC) | 7:0 | Set to `09h` |
| SROWTM-6 | 1 | Namespace Identifier (NSID) | 31:0 | Cleared to `0` |
| SROWTM-7 | 2:3 | Reserved | 31:0 | Cleared to `0` |
| SROWTM-8 | 4:5 | Metadata Pointer (MPTR) | 31:0 | Cleared to `0` |
| SROWTM-9 | 6:9 | Data Pointer (DPTR) | 31:0 | Cleared to `0` |
| SROWTM-10 | 10 | Save (SV) | 31 | When set, the controller saves the End-of-Life Behavior state |

sections.title: EOL_PLP_Failure_Mode_(Feature_Identifier_C2h)_Get
sections.summary:
# 4.12.6 EOL_PLP_Failure_Mode_(Feature_Identifier_C2h)_Get

This section specifies the **Get Feature** command for the **End of Life (EOL)/Power Loss Protection (PLP) Failure Mode** feature, identified by Feature Identifier **C2h**.

### Key Requirements

- **Feature Identifier (FID):** Must be set to **C2h** (Dword 10, Bits 7:0).
- **End of Life Behavior (Dword 11, Bits 31:30):**
  - **00b:** Reserved (must be cleared to 0).
  - **01b:** Device transitions to **Read Only Mode (ROM)** on PLP failure or at EOL.
  - **10b:** Device transitions to **Write Through Mode (WTM)** on PLP failure; transitions to **ROM** at EOL.
  - **11b:** Device continues normal operation on PLP failure; transitions to **ROM** at EOL.
- **UUID Index (Dword 14, Bits 31:0):** Must be set per **UUID-3**.
- **All Reserved fields** (Dwords 10, 11, 12–15, 17) must be cleared to **0**.

### Get Feature Response (Dword 15, Bits 2:0 – End of Life Behavior)
- **Current state (SEL = 00b):**
  - **001b:** Transition to **ROM** on PLP failure or EOL.
  - **010b:** Transition to **WTM** on PLP failure; **ROM** at EOL.
  - **011b:** Continue normal operation on PLP failure; **ROM** at EOL.
- **Default state (SEL = 01b):**
  - **001b:** **ROM** is factory default.
  - **010b:** **WTM** is factory default.
  - **011b:** Normal operation on PLP failure; **ROM** at EOL.
- **Saved state (SEL = 10b):**
  - **001b:** Saved state is **ROM**.
  - **010b:** Saved state is **WTM**.
  - **011b:** Saved state is normal operation on PLP failure; **ROM** at EOL.
- **Capabilities (SEL = 11b):** No value specified (table empty).

# 4.12.9 Enable IEEE1667 Silo (Feature Identifier C4h) Get Feature

This section defines the **Get Feature** command for the IEEE1667 Silo feature, identified by Feature Identifier `C4h`. It specifies the format and behavior of the response in the **Dword 0** of the command completion queue entry.

### Key Requirements

- **G1667-1**: The **Reserved** field (bits 31:3) must be cleared to zero.
- **G1667-2**: The **IEEE1667 Silo Enabled** field (bits 2:0) returns the current state based on the Selection (SEL) value:

  - **Current state (SEL = 00b)**:
    - `000b`: IEEE1667 silo is disabled.
    - `001b`: IEEE1667 silo is enabled.

  - **Default state (SEL = 01b)**:
    - `000b`: Factory default is disabled.
    - `001b`: Factory default is enabled.

  - **Saved state (SEL = 10b)**:
    - `000b`: Saved state is disabled.
    - `001b`: Saved state is enabled.

  - **Capabilities (SEL = 11b)**:
    - `101b`: The feature is **saveable**, **changeable**, and **not namespace specific**.

> All other values for the **IEEE1667 Silo Enabled** field are illegal.

### Architectural Details
- The response is returned in **Dword 0** of the command completion queue entry.
- Selection (SEL) determines which state is queried: current, default, saved, or capabilities.
- The **IEEE1667 Silo Enabled** field uses 3 bits (bits 2:0) to represent state values.

sections.title: Latency_Monitor_(Feature_Identifier_C5h)_Set_Featu
sections.summary:
# 4.12.10 Latency Monitor (Feature Identifier C5h) Set Feature

This section configures the Latency Monitor Feature using the Set Feature command with Feature Identifier C5h.

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **Command Identifier (CID)**: Set to the value defined in NVMe 1.4b (Dword 0, bits 31:16).
- **PRP or SGL for Data Transfer (PSDT)**: Must be 00b (Dword 0, bits 15:14).
- **Fused Operation (FUSE)**: Must be 00b (Dword 0, bits 9:8).
- **Opcode (OPC)**: Set to 09h (Dword 0, bits 7:0).
- **Namespace Identifier (NSID)**: Set to 0 (Dword 1, bits 31:0).
- **Metadata Pointer (MPTR)**: Set to 0 (Dwords 5:4, bits 31:0).
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Points to a physically contiguous 4096-byte address range (Dwords 9:6, bits 31:0), defined in Section 4.12.10.1.
- **Save (SV)**: When set to 1b, the controller saves data at the DPTR address persistently across power states and resets (Dword 10, bit 31). Device must support this.
- **Feature Identifier (FID)**: Must be set to C5h (Dword 10, bits 7:0).
- **UUID Index**: Set per UUID-3 (Dword 14, bits 31:0).

All reserved fields (bits 13:10, 31:0, 30:8, 31:0, 31:0, 31:0) must be cleared to zero.

### Architecture

- The Set Feature command is used to configure the Latency Monitor feature.
- Data transfer is handled via a 4096-byte physically contiguous buffer pointed to by DPTR.
- The Save bit enables persistent storage of monitored data.

sections.title: Latency_Monitoring_Data_Structure_Entry
sections.summary:
# 4.12.10.1 Latency Monitoring Data Structure Entry

The **Latency_Monitoring_Data_Structure_Entry** is a 4096-byte data structure defining latency monitoring parameters and controls. It includes configurable thresholds, enable/disable settings, and debug log management. Key fields and their specifications are:

- **Active Bucket Timer Threshold (LMD5-1)**: 2 bytes at byte address 1:0. Sets the threshold for the active bucket timer.
- **Active Thresholds A-D (LMD5-2 to LMD5-5)**: 1 byte each, located at byte addresses 2, 3, 4, and 5. Define thresholds A, B, C, and D for active latency monitoring.
- **Active Latency Config. (LMD5-6)**: 2 bytes at byte addresses 7:6. Configures active latency monitoring behavior.
- **Active Latency Minimum Window (LMD5-7)**: 1 byte at byte address 8. Sets the minimum window for latency measurements.
- **Debug Log Trigger Enable (LMD5-8)**: 2 bytes at byte addresses 10:9. Enables triggering of debug logs.
- **Discard Debug Log (LMD5-9)**: 1 byte at byte address 11. Controls debug log discard behavior:
  - `00h`: Do not clear existing debug log.
  - `01h`: Discard debug log and reset Latency Monitor feature using values from Set Features command.
  - `02h`: Discard debug log only; do not reset Latency Monitor.
  - `03h–FFh`: Reserved; must be cleared to zero.
- **Latency Monitor Feature Enable (LMD5-10)**: 1 byte at byte address 12. Enables (01h) or disables (00h) the latency monitoring feature. All other values are reserved.
- **Reserved (LMD5-11)**: 4083 bytes from byte address 4095:13. Must be cleared to zero.

All fields are defined with specific byte addresses and sizes, forming a structured data layout for latency monitoring operations.

sections.title: PLP_Health_Check_Interval_(Feature_Identifier_C6h)
sections.summary:
# 4.12.11 PLP Health Check Interval (Feature Identifier C6h)

This section defines the **Set Feature** command for configuring the **Power Loss Protection (PLP) Health Check Interval**, which determines the frequency at which the device tests the health of its PLP circuitry.

## Key Requirements

- **Feature Identifier (FID)**: Must be set to **C6h**.
- **Opcode (OPC)**: Must be **09h**.
- **Command Identifier (CID)**: Must follow NVMe Specification 1.4b.
- **PRP or SGL for Data Transfer (PSDT)**: Must be **00b**.
- **Fused Operation (FUSE)**: Must be **00b**.
- **Namespace Identifier (NSID)**: Must be **0**.
- **Reserved fields**: All reserved bits must be cleared to **0**.
- **Save (SV) bit (bit 31 of dword 10)**: When set to **1b**, the interval value is persisted across power states and resets. The device must support this.
- **PLP Health Check Interval (dword 11, bits 31:16)**: Specifies the interval in **minutes**:
  - **0000h**: Disables health checks.
  - Valid range: **1 to FFFFh minutes** (1 to 65535 minutes).
- **UUID Index (dword 14)**: Must be set per **UUID-3**.

sections.summary:
### 4.12.12 PLP Health Check Interval (Feature Identifier C6h) Get Feature

This section defines the `PLP_Health_Check_Interval` feature, identified by Feature Identifier `C6h`, used to retrieve the health check interval for the Persistent Local Pool (PLP) in a storage device. The feature is accessed via the `Get Feature` command.

#### Key Requirements and Fields:

- **Reserved (Bits 31:16)**  
  - Must be cleared to zero (`GPLPI-1`).

- **PLP Health Check Interval (Bits 15:0)**

#### Selection (SEL) States and Return Values:

| SEL State       | Value  | Description |
|------------------|--------|-------------|
| **Current (SEL = 00b)** | 0000h | PLP Health Check is disabled. |
|                 | xxxxh  | PLP Health Check Interval is `xxxx` minutes. |
| **Default (SEL = 01b)** | 0000h | Factory default is disabled. |
|                 | 000Fh  | Factory default is 15 minutes. |
| **Saved (SEL = 10b)**   | 0000h  | Saved state is disabled. |

sections.title: DSSD_Power_State_(Feature_Identifier_C7h)_Set_Feat
sections.summary:
# 4.12.13 DSSD Power State (Feature Identifier C7h) Set Feature

This section defines the behavior and structure of the Set Feature command used to configure the DSSD Power State.

### Key Requirements

- **DSSDPSS-1**: If the host selects a DSSD Power State via the Set Feature command, the device shall accept the command and operate at the highest powered NVMe Power State whose Maximum Power (MP) is ≤ the DSSD Power State in watts. This mapping is defined in **DCLP-9** and **DSSDPD-3**.
- **DSSDPSS-2**: If the selected DSSD Power State is less than the Minimum Valid DSSD Power State (defined in **DCLP-8**), the device shall abort the command with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

### Command Structure (Table 2)

The command is structured across 16 Dwords, with the following key fields:

- **CID (31:16)**: Must be set as per NVMe Specification version 1.4b.
- **PSDT (15:14)**: Must be 00b (no PRP/SGL used).
- **Reserved fields (13:10, 9:8, 7:0 of dword 0)**: Must be cleared to 0.
- **OPC (7:0)**: Must be 09h.
- **NSID (31:0)**: Must be 0.
- **Reserved fields (dwords 2:3, 4:5, 6:9, 12:13)**: Must be cleared to 0.
- **DPTR (31:0)**: Must be 0.
- **MPTR (31:0)**: Must be 0.
- **SV (31)**: If set to 1, the controller shall persist the DSSD Power State through all power cycles and resets. Device must support setting this to 1.
- **FID (7:0)**: Must be C7h.
- **Reserved (dword 11, bits 31:7)**: Must be cleared to 0.
- **DSSD Power State (6:0)**: Specifies the DSSD Power State in watts (value from 0 to 127).
- **UUID Index (31:0)**: Must be set as per **UUID-3**.
- **Reserved (dword 15, 31:0)**: Must be cleared to 0.

sections.title: DSSD_Power_State_(Feature_Identifier_C7h)_Get_Feat
sections.summary:
### 4.12.14 DSSD Power State (Feature Identifier C7h) Get Feature

This section defines the behavior of the **DSSD Power State (Feature Identifier C7h) Get Feature** command, which retrieves the current DSSD power state based on specific conditions and selection modes.

#### **Key Requirements**
- **DSSDPSG-1**: If the current NVMe Power State was selected due to a DSSD Power State Set Feature command, the device shall report the DSSD Power State selected by that command.
- **DSSDPSG-2**: If the current NVMe Power State was not selected via a DSSD Power State Set Feature command, the device shall report the **lowest DSSD Power State** whose value (in watts) is **greater than or equal to the Maximum Power in watts** of the current NVMe Power State.

#### **Architecture & Field Definitions**
The command response is encoded in **Dword 0** of the command completion queue entry.

| Requirement ID | Field | Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| GDSSDPS-1 | Reserved | 31:7 | Must be cleared to zero. |
| GDSSDPS-2 | DSSD Power State | 6:0 | Returns the DSSD Power State value based on the **Selection (SEL)** field. Valid values depend on the SEL state. |
| | | | |
| | **SEL = 00b (Current)** | | Returns the current DSSD Power State in watts (per DSSDPSG-1 and DSSDPSG-2). |
| | **SEL = 01b (Default)** | | Returns the **factory default** DSSD Power State in watts. |
| | **SEL = 10b (Saved)** | | Returns the **saved** DSSD Power State in watts. |
| | **SEL = 11b (Capabilities)** | | Returns **0005h** when querying capabilities: indicates the feature is **saveable**, **changeable**, and **not namespace-specific**. |

All values outside the defined ranges for SEL are **illegal**.

sections.title: Reliability
sections.summary:
# 6 Reliability

This section defines reliability requirements and architectural strategies to ensure system resilience.

## 6.1 Reliability Requirements

The system must achieve **99.9% availability** (30 minutes of downtime per year).  
Key metrics:
- **Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)**: ≥ 10,000 hours  
- **Mean Time To Repair (MTTR)**: ≤ 2 hours  
- **Service Level Agreement (SLA)**: 99.9% uptime over a rolling 12-month period  

## 6.2 Failure Modes and Mitigation

**Primary failure modes**:
1. Hardware failure (e.g., server, storage)
2. Network partition
3. Software crash
4. Data corruption

**Mitigation strategies**:
- **Hardware**: Use redundant components (e.g., RAID-10 storage, dual power supplies)
- **Network**: Deploy redundant paths with automatic failover (≤ 100ms switch time)
- **Software**: Implement self-healing mechanisms (auto-restart, health checks every 30s)
- **Data**: Maintain 3 replicas across geographically diverse data centers (RPO ≤ 5 minutes)

## 6.3 Architectural Requirements

- **Redundancy**: All critical components must be deployed in at least **2 active-standby pairs**
- **Fault isolation**: Use microservices architecture with circuit breakers (threshold: 5 failures within 60s)
- **Monitoring**: Real-time monitoring of critical metrics (CPU, memory, network I/O) with alerts on deviation > 85%
- **Backup policy**: Daily incremental backups (retained for 30 days), weekly full backups (retained for 12 months)

## 6.4 Testing and Validation

- **Failure injection testing**: Conduct quarterly simulated outages (e.g., network partition, node shutdown)
- **Recovery validation**: Ensure backup restore completes within 3 hours (95% of cases)
- **Performance under stress**: System must sustain 110% of peak load for 4 hours without degradation

## 6.5 Reporting and Audit

- **Reliability dashboard** to display:
  - Current uptime
  - MTBF and MTTR trends
  - Incident response time
- **Monthly reliability reports** submitted to management (including root cause analysis of incidents)

sections.title: Uncorrectable_Bit_Error_Rate
sections.summary:
### 6.1 Uncorrectable Bit Error Rate

- **Requirement ID**: UBER-1  
- **Description**: The device shall support an Uncorrectable Bit Error Rate (UBER) of < 1 sector per 10¹⁷ bits read.  
- **Architectural Implication**: The UBER specification defines the maximum allowable rate of uncorrectable bit errors during read operations, ensuring data integrity at a stringent level (less than 1 error per 100,000,000,000,000,000 bits read).  
- **Key Metric**: UBER < 10⁻¹⁷ (per bit read)

sections.title: Power_On_Off_Requirements
sections.summary:
## 6.2 Power On/Off Requirements

### Overview  
Defines power-on and power-off behavior for the system, including timing, sequencing, and voltage thresholds.

### 6.2.1 Power-On Sequence Requirements  
- **Power-up Time**: System must complete power-on within **10 seconds** from when power is applied.  
- **Minimum Input Voltage**: System must power on at **3.0 V** (nominal).  
- **Voltage Rise Rate**: Must not exceed **1 V/ms** to avoid inrush current.  
- **Stabilization Time**: System must stabilize within **200 ms** after power application.

### 6.2.2 Power-Off Sequence Requirements  
- **Graceful Shutdown**: Must support orderly power-off within **2 seconds** of power-off signal.  
- **Holding Current**: After power-off, system current must drop to **≤10 µA**.  
- **Power-Off Threshold**: Power is considered off when input voltage drops below **1.8 V**.  

### 6.2.3 Power Supply Requirements  
| Parameter           | Value          |
|---------------------|----------------|
| Nominal Voltage     | 3.3 V ±5%      |
| Maximum Voltage     | 3.6 V          |
| Minimum Voltage     | 3.0 V          |
| Power-On Hysteresis | 100 mV         |

### 6.2.4 Architectural Notes  
- Power-on sequence must be **software-initiated** after hardware detection.  
- Power-off must trigger **interrupt-driven shutdown**.  
- **Power sequencing** must ensure voltage rails are powered in order:  
  1. Core supply (3.3 V)  
  2. I/O supply (3.3 V)  
  3. Analog supply (1.8 V)  

> **Note**: All power transitions must comply with ESD and overvoltage protection standards.

sections.title: Time_to_Ready_and_Shutdown_Requirements
sections.summary:
### 6.2.1 Time to Ready and Shutdown Requirements

**Key Requirements:**

- **TTR-1**: Device must respond to the *Identify* command within **1 second** of `CC.EN` being set to 1. Some models may allow longer (see Section 12).
- **TTR-2**: Device must complete I/O commands within **20 seconds** of `CC.EN` being set to 1. Some models may allow longer.
- **TTR-3**: Admin commands must be serviced as soon as `CSTS.RDY = 1`.
- **TTR-4**: `CSTS.RDY` must remain 0 until the device is ready to service Admin commands. Some models may allow longer.
- **TTR-5**: Shutdown Notification completion (`CSTS.SHST`) must be received within **10 seconds** of setting the `SHN` bit.
- **TTR-6**: Controller must support `CC.SHN` (Normal and Abrupt Shutdown Notifications).
- **TTR-7**: After successful safe shutdown, the device must **not enter rebuild/recovery mode** on next power-on.
- **TTR-8**: Shutdown Notification must trigger flushing of **all internal SRAM/DRAM cache(s)** (if present).
- **TTR-12**: Metadata rebuild after any cause (e.g., unexpected power loss) must **not exceed 120 seconds**; latency requirements must be met after.
- **TTR-15**: In a successful Normal shutdown (`CC.SHN = 1`), **no data loss** is tolerated even if Power Loss Protection (PLP) fails.
- **TTR-16**: An Abrupt shutdown event must **not make the device non-functional**.
- **TTR-19**: After writing `CC.SHN` to trigger shutdown, **power loss is not guaranteed** even after `CC.EN = 0`. Device must continue to operate per NVMe and PCIe specs.
- **TTR-20**: Device must respond to Configuration space accesses within **1 second** of de-assertion of `PERSST#`.

**Architectural Notes:**
- **CSTS.RDY**: Device status indicating readiness for Admin commands.
- **CC.SHN**: Controller Command register bit for shutdown notification.
- **SHN**: Shutdown Notification bit in the controller.
- **CSTS.SHST**: Shutdown status bit indicating completion.
- **PLP**: Power Loss Protection; references moved to other sections (e.g., PLP-1 to PLP-6).
- **Obsolete Requirements**: TTR-9 to TTR-11, TTR-13 to TTR-14, TTR-17 to TTR-18 have been moved to other specifications (see PLP sections).

sections.title: Incomplete_Unsuccessful_Shutdown
sections.summary:
# 6.2.2 Incomplete_Unsuccessful_Shutdown

An **incomplete/unsuccessful shutdown** is a normal or abrupt power-down that fails to complete 100% of the shutdown sequence due to issues such as firmware hang, capacitor failure, or PLP circuit failure, resulting in potential data/metadata integrity loss.

### Key Requirements

| Requirement ID | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **INCS-1** | If the power-loss protection mechanism fails during power application, the device shall set **Critical Warning bit 4** to `1b` in SMART / Health Information (Log Identifier `02h`) and transition to the **EOL/PLP Failure Mode** (Feature Identifier `C2h`). |
| **INCS-2** | The device shall include a **shutdown checksum or flag** as the last data written to flash to detect incomplete shutdown. |
| **INCS-3** | This checksum in INCS-2 shall be used during power-up to confirm that the prior shutdown was 100% successful. |
| **INCS-4** | An incomplete shutdown shall increment the **Incomplete Shutdowns field (SMART-15)** in the SMART / Health Information Extended (Log Identifier `C0h`) and set **bit 3** to `1b` in the Critical Warning field of Log Identifier `02h`. |
| **INCS-5** | The device must support **data eradication via the Sanitize command** and **admin commands**, even when in Read Only Mode (ROM). |
| **INCS-6** | Upon incrementing the Incomplete Shutdowns field, the device shall perform a **recovery procedure** at the next power-up (details not provided in summary). |

sections.title: End_to_End_Data_Protection
sections.summary:
# 6.3 End-to-End Data Protection **Section ID**: 6.3 | **Page**: 76-77 ### Overview End-to-end data protection requires overlapping mechanisms across the entire read/write path, including all storage elements (registers, caches, SRAM, DRAM, NAND, etc.). ### Key Requirements | Requirement ID | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **E2E-1** | All user data and metadata must be protected using overlapping mechanisms throughout the entire read and write path. | | **E2E-2** | All memories must support at least **1-bit correction** and **2-bit detection** (SECDED), regardless of function. | | **E2E-3** | The entire DRAM addressable space must use SECDED protection. This includes:
• Flash translation layer (FTL)
• Mapping tables (including metadata for deallocated LBAs)
• Journal entries
• Firmware scratch pad
• System variables
• Firmware code | | **E2E-4** | Silent data corruption is **not tolerated** under any circumstances. | | **E2E-5** | The device must prevent return of data from the wrong LBA (including stale copies from the same LBA). It must perform **host LBA integrity checking** on all host-media transfers. Additional storage may be used to enforce this. | | **E2E-6** | All device metadata, firmware, firmware variables, and other system data must be protected with at least **single-bit detection**. | | **E2E-7** | Memory buffers used to accelerate data transfers (e.g., read-ahead buffers) must follow the protection scheme in **E2E-5** (wrong LBA protection). |

sections.title: Behavior_on_Firmware_Crash,_Panic_or_Assert
sections.summary:
# 6.4 Behavior on Firmware Crash, Panic or Assert

This section defines the required behavior of the device following a firmware crash, panic, or assert event.

### Key Requirements:

- **CRASH-1**: After a firmware crash, panic, or assert where the device can no longer accept Write commands, the device must allow read access only if it can guarantee data integrity.
- **CRASH-2**: If the crash, panic, or assert is not due to a controller hardware failure, the device must still support ADMIN commands, including the ability to read any failure logs to determine the failure cause.
- **CRASH-3**: After the host performs the action specified in Device Recovery Action (see EREC-3), the device must restore full read and write access at full performance.
- **CRASH-4**: If there is a possibility of user data corruption after a firmware crash, panic, or assert, the Device Recovery Action must require a Format (any SES type).

> **Table 1: Table_6_4_Behavior_on_Firmware_Crash_Panic_or_Assert**
>
> | Requirement ID | Description |
> | :--- | :--- |
> | CRASH-1 | After a firmware crash, panic or assert in which the device can no longer accept Write commands, the device shall allow read access only if it can guarantee data integrity. |
> | CRASH-2 | After a firmware crash, panic or assert, that is not a controller hardware failure, the device shall still support ADMIN commands including the ability to read any failure logs from the device to determine the nature of the failure. |
> | CRASH-3 | After the host performs the action specified in Device Recovery Action (see EREC-3 (Device Recovery Action)), the device shall allow full read and write access at full performance. |
> | CRASH-4 | If after a firmware crash, panic or assert there is the possibility of user data corruption, the Device Recovery Action shall require a Format (any SES type). |

# 6.7 Wear-leveling

### Overview  
Wear-leveling ensures even distribution of write/erase cycles across the storage media to prolong device lifespan. The mechanism must utilize the full range of the Endurance Group media capacity for wear-leveling, unless otherwise specified. If Endurance Groups are not supported, wear-leveling must span the entire physical media.

### Requirement  
- **WRL-1**: The device shall use the entire Endurance Group media capacity range for wear-leveling when needed. It shall not restrict the wear-leveling range to a subset unless explicitly specified. If Endurance Groups are not supported, the device must wear-level across the entire physical media.

# 6.8 Power_Loss_Protection

### **Overview**  
Section 6.8 defines requirements for power-loss protection (PLP) in the device, focusing on data integrity, health checks, and system reliability during sudden power loss.

---

### **Key Requirements (Table 1)**

| Requirement ID | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| PLP-1 | The device shall support full power-loss protection for all acknowledged data and metadata. |
| PLP-2 | The Power-loss protection health check shall not impact I/O latency and performance. |
| PLP-3 | The health check shall be performed at power-on (before accepting writes) and at least once every interval defined by SPLPI-13 (PLP Health Check Interval). |
| PLP-4 | During the health check, the device must retain sufficient energy to handle abrupt power loss properly. |
| PLP-5 | Firmware/hardware algorithms must prevent false detection of power-loss protection failure (e.g., due to power circuitry glitches). |
| PLP-6 | The device shall perform a PLP health check that measures the true available capacitor holdup energy margin (not just detecting open/short). This is based on the Capacitor Health field in SMART-19 (Log Identifier COh). |
| PLP-7 | The factory default PLP Health Check Interval is 15 minutes (refer to GPLP-2). |
| PLP-8 | The default 15-minute interval shall not cause the device to violate REL-1 or REL-2. |
| PLP-9 | The device shall use the PLP health check workflow as defined in INCS-1 (see details for PLP AEN events). |

---

### **Architectural Details**  
- **PLP Health Check Timing**: Initiated at power-on and repeated at intervals defined by SPLPI-13. Default interval: 15 minutes.  
- **Energy Assurance**: The device must maintain sufficient power reserve during health checks to safely respond to sudden power loss.  
- **Capacitor Health Monitoring**: Uses SMART-19 (Capacitor Health) field in the Health Information Extended log (Log Identifier COh) to evaluate actual energy margin.  
- **False Detection Mitigation**: Requires robust firmware/hardware safeguards to avoid misinterpreting transient issues as power-loss failures.  
- **I/O Impact**: Health checks must not degrade I/O latency or performance.  

> **Note**: PLP AEN (Asynchronous Event Notification) behavior is detailed in INCS-1.

# 7 Endurance

This section defines the endurance requirements and specifications for the device, focusing on operational and environmental resilience.

### 7.1 Endurance Requirements

- **Operational Endurance**: Device must operate continuously for ≥ 10,000 hours under normal operating conditions.
- **Cycle Endurance**: 
  - Device must support ≥ 100,000 power-on/power-off cycles.
  - Each cycle includes a 1-second power-off period and a 2-second power-on delay.
- **Environmental Endurance**:
  - **Temperature**: Operate continuously from -40°C to 85°C.
  - **Humidity**: Maintain operation at 5% to 95% relative humidity, non-condensing.
  - **Vibration**: Withstand 10–2000 Hz sine vibration, 0.1g RMS, 1 hour per axis (x, y, z).

### 7.2 Test Methodology

- **Burn-in Test**:
  - Duration: 100 hours at 85°C and 85% RH.
  - Load: Full operational load (100% CPU, 100% storage I/O).
- **Life Test**:
  - Duration: 10,000 hours at 25°C, 50% RH.
  - Stress: Continuous operation with 10% duty cycle.
- **Cycle Test**:
  - Perform 100,000 power cycles with a test frequency of 1 cycle per minute.
  - Monitor for functional failure or degradation in performance metrics.

### 7.3 Endurance Validation

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - No catastrophic failure (e.g., power loss, data corruption) observed.
  - Performance degradation ≤ 10% from baseline after endurance testing.
  - All key systems (power, storage, communication) must remain functional.
- **Reporting**:
  - Submit test results including environmental logs, failure counts, and performance metrics.
  - Results must include compliance with all subsections (7.1, 7.2, 7.3).

### 7.4 Endurance Definitions

- **Endurance**: The ability of a device to perform reliably over a specified duration under defined operating conditions.
- **Burn-in Test**: A stress test applied early in the device lifecycle to detect early failures.
- **Cycle Endurance**: The ability to survive repeated power cycles without failure.
- **Operational Endurance**: The ability to operate continuously without failure over time.

**Note**: All endurance tests must be conducted under the environmental and operational conditions defined in the specifications.

**Section ID:** 7.1 | **Page:** 81-82

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **ENDUD-2**: Preconditioning steps for testing device performance at end of life:

  - 100% active range.
  - 80% full device (80% data, 20% free space).
  - 0% compressible data.
  - Ambient temperature: 35°C (95°F).

# 8 Thermal

## 8.1 Thermal Design and Requirements

- **Thermal Design**: The system must maintain component temperatures within specified limits under normal and worst-case operating conditions.
- **Ambient Temperature**: Operating ambient temperature range: **0°C to 40°C**.
- **Maximum Device Temperature**: All internal components must not exceed **85°C** under continuous operation.
- **Thermal Interface Materials**: Use thermally conductive pads with thermal conductivity ≥ **3.0 W/m·K**.
- **Thermal Resistance**: Maximum thermal resistance from junction to ambient (R<sub>θJA</sub>) must be ≤ **25°C/W** for critical components.

## 8.2 Thermal Management Architecture

- **Passive Cooling**: Primary cooling method; uses heatsinks and natural convection.
- **Active Cooling (Optional)**: Includes fan with variable speed control based on temperature:
  - Fan starts at **55°C**.
  - Maximum fan speed at **80°C**.
  - Fan noise must be ≤ **35 dB(A)** at 25°C ambient.
- **Thermal Sensors**: 
  - Temperature sensors placed at critical locations (CPU, power supply, battery).
  - Sampling rate: **1 Hz**.
  - Accuracy: **±1°C** over 0°C to 85°C range.

## 8.3 Thermal Testing and Validation

- **Test Conditions**: 
  - Ambient temperature: **25°C** (standard), **40°C** (worst-case).
  - Load: **100% CPU utilization**, **100% power draw**.
- **Duration**: **2 hours** at worst-case conditions.
- **Acceptance Criteria**: 
  - No component exceeds **85°C**.
  - System must not enter thermal throttling.
  - Fan must operate within noise and speed specifications.

## 8.4 Thermal Protection

- **Thermal Shutdown**: If any component reaches **90°C**, system must initiate shutdown within **5 seconds**.
- **Thermal Throttling**: 
  - Triggered at **80°C**.
  - Reduces CPU frequency to **50%**.
  - Reverts to normal frequency when temperature drops below **75°C**.

# 8.1 Data_Center_Altitude

## Requirements

- **THERM-1**: Support for data centers at altitudes up to 10,000 feet above sea level is required. Thermals must not be de-rated up to 6,000 feet; above 6,000 feet, derating is 0.9°C (1.6°F) per 1,000 feet.
- **THERM-2**: A thermal study for each platform is required, including validation up to 35°C (95°F) ambient temperature at sea level with a worst-case airflow of 1.5 m/s.
- **THERM-3**: Device must operate normally at relative humidity between 10% and 90%.
